prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. The board's rules allowed only its finance committee to place a spending request on the agenda, and she chaired that committee for the whole decade. Department heads seeking a new ward or a costly machine sent their requests to the committee, which met in her office; of the forty or so requests that arrived each year, about five reached the full board, and the trustees approved nearly every one they saw. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: Only her committee could put spending on the agenda, and only about five of forty requests a year got past it to a board that approved almost all it saw, so she controlled what reached the board: its "gatekeeper." "Figurehead" fails because that control was real power, not a title without it. "Envoy" fails because her work was screening requests coming in, not representing the board to anyone outside it. "Holdout" fails because she was not resisting a decision the other trustees had reached.

figurehead.quote: about five reached the full board
figurehead.why: her committee decided which requests the board ever saw, which is real power, the opposite of an empty title

envoy.quote: sent their requests to the committee
envoy.why: the traffic runs from department heads in to her; she carries nothing out to outside parties

holdout.quote: the trustees approved nearly every one they saw
holdout.why: the board agreed with what she sent; there is no majority she refused to join

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. She was elected the board's chair in 1961 and reelected every year after, and her name headed its letterhead. The bylaws let the chair vote only to break a tie, and the agenda and budget came each year from the hospital's administrator, whose recommendations the other eight trustees, almost always of one mind, adopted meeting after meeting. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: She held the chair and the letterhead, but she could vote only on a tie among trustees who almost always agreed, and the administrator set the agenda, so she was the board's "figurehead": its nominal head without power. "Gatekeeper" fails because the administrator, not she, decided what came before the board. "Envoy" fails because nothing she did carried the board's business to outsiders. "Holdout" fails because a chair who votes only on ties, among trustees of one mind, never casts a vote against the others.

gatekeeper.quote: the agenda and budget came each year from the hospital's administrator
gatekeeper.why: someone else controlled what reached the board, so she controlled no access

envoy.why: her role was a title and a name inside the board; no mission to outside parties is described

holdout.quote: vote only to break a tie
holdout.why: her only vote came on ties, and trustees almost always of one mind left none, so she could not stand against them

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. The hospital depended on a yearly grant from the state health department and on a road the county commissioners maintained to its door. Each spring for the whole decade the trustees settled in closed session on what to ask of both, and she then spent several weeks in the capital and the county seat. The board's minutes for each summer record it debating the officials' replies, which she read into the record herself. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: The trustees decided what to ask, she then spent weeks where the state and county officials sat, and the replies the board debated came back through her, so she was its "envoy," the representative it sent to outside parties. "Gatekeeper" fails because she did not decide what the board considered; the trustees settled the requests and debated the replies. "Figurehead" fails because weeks of dealing with officials was real work, not a title. "Holdout" fails because she carried requests the trustees had agreed on together.

gatekeeper.quote: the trustees settled in closed session
gatekeeper.why: the whole board chose what to ask and debated what came back; she screened nothing

figurehead.quote: spent several weeks in the capital and the county seat
figurehead.why: weeks of work with officials on the board's behalf is substantive, not ceremonial

holdout.why: the requests were settled by the trustees together, and she acted on them rather than refusing them

worlds.passage: For most of the 1960s a retired surgeon sat on the nine-member board of trustees of a county hospital. In 1962 the state invited every county hospital to join a pool for buying drugs and equipment, and the board voted eight to one to join. She voted no again, alone, at each of the four yearly renewals that followed, arguing that the pool's suppliers were too far away to deliver in an emergency, and she was still voting no in 1967, when every other county hospital renewed without dissent. In an oral history recorded decades later, one fellow trustee called her the board's ______ during those years.
worlds.explanation: The board joined by eight to one and renewed every year, and she alone kept voting no for five years while every other board in the county agreed, so she was the board's "holdout." "Gatekeeper" fails because her votes controlled nothing: the hospital joined and renewed regardless. "Figurehead" fails because she acted on her own judgment rather than lending a name to others' decisions. "Envoy" fails because she opposed the board's majority rather than representing it to outsiders.

gatekeeper.quote: the board voted eight to one to join
gatekeeper.why: the hospital joined over her vote, so nothing depended on her letting it through

figurehead.quote: arguing that the pool's suppliers were too far away
figurehead.why: she pressed her own reasoned position, not a title without a voice

envoy.why: she acted against the board's majority, not on its behalf toward outsiders
